blueprint_concepts: parabola from the focus-directrix definition with a general axis

concept_use.Locus based questions: The locus of P is found by translating the tangency condition into an equation in h, k.
concept_use.parabola from the focus-directrix defini: The locus is recognised as the parabola with focus O and directrix x+y=8 (oblique axis y=x); its latus rectum is twice the focus-directrix distance.

english: Let $O$ be the origin. A point $P$, different from $O$, moves in the plane in such a way that the circle drawn on $OP$ as a diameter always touches the line $x+y=4$. Then the length of the latus rectum of the locus of $P$ is equal to
hindi: माना $O$ मूल बिन्दु है। एक बिन्दु $P$, जो $O$ से भिन्न है, समतल में इस प्रकार गति करता है कि $OP$ को व्यास मानकर खींचा गया वृत्त सदैव रेखा $x+y=4$ को स्पर्श करता है। तब $P$ के बिन्दुपथ के नाभिलम्ब की लम्बाई बराबर है
solution: Let $P(h,k)$. The circle on $OP$ has centre $\left(\frac h2,\frac k2\right)$ and radius $\frac12\sqrt{h^2+k^2}$
So $OP$ = distance of $P$ from $x+y=8$: the locus is a parabola with focus $O$ and directrix $x+y=8$
Latus rectum $=2\times$(distance of focus from directrix) $=2\cdot\dfrac{8}{\sqrt2}=8\sqrt2$
solution_full: Let $P=(h,k)$. The circle with $OP$ as a diameter has centre $M\left(\frac h2,\frac k2\right)$, the midpoint of $OP$, and radius $\frac12 OP=\frac12\sqrt{h^2+k^2}$.
A circle touches a line exactly when the distance of its centre from the line equals its radius:

The left side is the distance of $P$ from the line $x+y=8$ and the right side is $OP$. So every position of $P$ is equidistant from the point $O$ and the line $x+y=8$, and conversely every such point gives a touching circle.
Hence the locus is a parabola with focus $O(0,0)$ and directrix $x+y=8$ (its axis is the line $y=x$, which is not parallel to a coordinate axis). Squaring gives the equation $(x-y)^2+16(x+y)-64=0$.
For a parabola, the semi-latus rectum equals the distance of the focus from the directrix, so the latus rectum is twice this distance.
Distance of $O$ from $x+y=8$ is $\dfrac{8}{\sqrt2}=4\sqrt2$, so the latus rectum is $8\sqrt2$.

Check: the chord through $O$ perpendicular to the axis is along $y=-x$; on it $P=(s,-s)$ has $OP=\sqrt2|s|$ and distance $\dfrac8{\sqrt2}$ from the directrix, so $|s|=4$ and the chord has length $2\cdot4\sqrt2=8\sqrt2$.
originality_note: New: the locus is generated by a tangency condition on the circle with diameter OP (way 5: diametric circle + focus-directrix), which turns into the focus-directrix property with the directrix at twice the distance of the given line. Closest known: locus of the centre of a circle through a fixed point touching a fixed line. Different because: the moving point is an end of the diameter, so the directrix is x+y=8, not the given line, and the parabola has an oblique axis.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, line, curve and symbol is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath (and a numerical brute-force check), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Stated that P is different from O (the circle degenerates at O). Changed: added 'different from O'.
key_step: Halving the tangency condition shows OP equals the distance of P from x+y=8, a parabola with focus O.
justification: A short chain of standard facts (tangency, focus-directrix definition, latus rectum = 2 x focus-directrix distance) with one recognition step. Comparable to the routine conic chains of 2026-P2-Q2 (L2).
